title: Trump Creates First-Ever US Space Academy!
summary:
Guess what? The United States is getting its very first Space Academy! President Trump announced it on Friday at NASA's Johnson Space Center in Texas. He was there to honor the four astronauts who just flew around the moon.

Trump said the academy will be "a big deal" and "top line." It's like the Naval Academy or West Point, but for space! Those schools train young people to become military officers. This new academy will train students to work for the Space Force, NASA, and even the civilian flight industry.

A special commission will help create the academy. It will be led by NASA's boss, Jared Isaacman. Other important people are helping too, like Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth.

Trump also gave each of the four Artemis II astronauts a special medal called the Congressional Space Medal of Honor. It's the highest honor for space flight in the US. The astronauts are Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, Christina Koch, and Jeremy Hansen from Canada.

These astronauts did something amazing in April. They flew around the far side of the moon! That's farther than any humans have ever gone. Trump said he was in a meeting when he heard about it. "We actually had a television pulled up, and everybody was spellbound," he said.

The astronauts gave Trump a cool gift too—a blue flight jacket with the NASA logo. Victor Glover said, "And so here we have your jacket today."

This is a huge step for space exploration. Who knows? Maybe someday you could go to the Space Academy and become an astronaut!
why_it_matters: This matters because someday you could go to a school that turns space fans into real astronauts, pilots, or engineers.

background_read: President Donald Trump (the U.S. president) made the announcement at NASA (the American space agency).
The Naval Academy and West Point are famous U.S. military schools that train officers, and the new Space Academy will be similar but for space jobs.
Jared Isaacman (NASA's leader) will lead the group that plans it, and the four Artemis II astronauts (the crew of a moon mission) received a special medal for flying around the moon.
Article_Structure: WHO: President Trump, NASA's leader Jared Isaacman, Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, and the four Artemis II astronauts.
WHAT: Trump announced the creation of the first U.S. Space Academy and awarded the astronauts the Congressional Space Medal of Honor.
WHERE: NASA's Johnson Space Center in Texas.
WHY: To train students for Space Force, NASA, and the civilian flight industry, and to mark a major step in space exploration.

perspectives.description: They are excited because the Space Academy could train more astronauts and make space jobs feel possible for kids.
They may wonder how much the academy will cost and whether the government should spend money on other things first.
They point out that the academy is only the first step — a commission still has to plan it before it opens.
